synthesis.description: When a business is sold or handed over (HPL to AEP, then the North American gas and power trading business to UBS), staff circulate transition memos, lists of files and directories, rosters of traders, profit centers and procedures, and data copying protocols. Owners ask others to review memos and send changes, list which procedures the estate team must keep running, enter test deals after system cutovers, and copy compliant data to the new environment by a stated deadline such as midnight CST, Thursday, February 7, 2002.
steps: A coordinator circulates a memo or plan of transition issues and asks for review.
Desks list the files, directories, procedures and traders that move or stay.
Rosters, profit centers and status files for the new owner are compiled and sent.
Systems are separated and test deals are entered after databases come back up.
Staff copy permitted data and documents to the new environment by the deadline.
Remaining duties such as daily settlements are assigned to the estate team.
synthesis.approach: A shared transition tracker listing each file share, procedure, system and person with its destination (new owner or estate), status and owner would replace the repeated memos and roster requests, with a standard data-migration checklist for each desk.
synthesis.rationale: The rounds keep rebuilding the same lists of people, procedures, files and profit centers. One tracker layout gathers them once, makes review easier and shows what is still open.
